Synopsis:
Dialog between the player and Tolna. Tolna is responsible for everything book-related in the Sorcerous Sundries shop. Players can ask her about the high-end books, including the Carenthian cypher, which allows the player to read the last chapter of the Necromancy of Thay book. Players can pay a large sum for them.Tolna only speaks in whispers

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Tolna.json: Tolna is the Sorcerous Sundries shop’s literature specialist — she handles rare and restricted books and speaks only in a whisper. Players can ask her about high‑end texts (notably the Carenthian cypher, which lets you read the last chapter of the Necromancy of Thay) but those items are expensive and require a large payment. Her habit of shushing customers is presented as reverence for the books rather than fear or secrecy. The provided samples show routine shop questions (why whisper, any rare tomes, what do you have) and Tolna responding with the same quiet, librarian‑like admonition.
- FOR_DangerousBook_Tome.json: The player finds a book on necromancy - from one of the Red Wizards of Thay. Once read, the book will be bound to whoever tried to read it. Some origins will demand you let them read it, while others will want the book burned. If you read the book, you'll hear strange, distant whispers. The more you read, the stronger the voices will become, and the greater the chance that you'll be driven mad.
- CAMP_DangerousBook_IVB_CFM_Astarion.json: After giving Astarion the Tome of Thayan Necromancy, he begins to study it at camp to learn its secrets. He's frustrated by the voices of the spirits contained within the book, which are stopping him from accessing the secrets he's sure it contains. If he pushes the spirits too far, they'll respond with force - tearing at him with spectral hands. As you discuss the book with Astarion, his tone is on edge - nearly obsessive about discovering what's in the book. He won't part with it, even if he can't read it right now.
- LOW_SorcerousSundries_Rolan.json: Dialog with Sorcerous Sundries' clerk Rolan. He will explain how Lorroakan is neglecting him in his search for the Nightsong. Player can ask Rolan to make a portal to Lorroakan.
- SHA_Trials_PAD_ObjectOfDarknessHint.json: The player speaks up on entering one of the trial areas in the temple of Shar. If they had previously read a book in the library area, they'll have an idea of what they need to do (navigate the maze and get through the locked door on the far side without being detected/setting off a trap). Otherwise they'll be none the wiser.

The player finds a book on necromancy - from one of the Red Wizards of Thay. Once read, the book will be bound to whoever tried to read it. Some origins will demand you let them read it, while others will want the book burned. If you read the book, you'll hear strange, distant whispers. The more you read, the stronger the voices will become, and the greater the chance that you'll be driven mad.

After giving Astarion the Tome of Thayan Necromancy, he begins to study it at camp to learn its secrets. He's frustrated by the voices of the spirits contained within the book, which are stopping him from accessing the secrets he's sure it contains. If he pushes the spirits too far, they'll respond with force - tearing at him with spectral hands. As you discuss the book with Astarion, his tone is on edge - nearly obsessive about discovering what's in the book. He won't part with it, even if he can't read it right now.

context: Tolna is the Sorcerous Sundries shop’s literature specialist who handles rare and restricted books; she speaks only in a whisper and habitually shushes customers as an expression of reverence for the volumes. Players can ask her about high‑end texts — most notably the Carenthian cypher, which will let you read the final chapter of the Necromancy of Thay — but such items are costly and require a large payment. The Necromancy of Thay tome is dangerous: reading it can bind the book to the reader, draws forth distant whispering voices, and increases the risk of madness, so other characters who study it (for example Astarion in camp) can become obsessed or physically harmed by the spirits within. The example lines simply illustrate Tolna’s quiet, librarian‑like admonitions when customers ask about rare tomes.
